formulations.label: Film-coated tablets
formulations.strengths: 10 mg (the strength covered by the 10 mg film-coated tablet SmPC used here)

src.q: Each film-coated tablet contains 10 mg atorvastatin (as atorvastatin calcium trihydrate).

formulations.label: Chewable tablets
formulations.strengths: 10 mg (the strength covered by the 10 mg chewable tablet SmPC used here)
formulations.note: Same indications, doses and warnings as the film-coated tablets; can be chewed or swallowed whole. Contains aspartame (phenylalanine).

src.q: Each chewable tablet contains 10 mg atorvastatin (as atorvastatin calcium trihydrate).
Lipitor chewable tablets can be chewed or swallowed whole with a drink of water
Lipitor chewable tablet contains aspartame which is a source of phenylalanine. May be harmful for people with phenylketonuria.

items.t: Adjunct to diet to lower total-C, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B and triglycerides in primary hypercholesterolaemia (including heterozygous familial) or mixed hyperlipidaemia, in adults and children aged 10 years or older, when diet and other measures are not enough.

src.q: in adults, adolescents and children aged 10 years or older with primary hypercholesterolaemia including familial hypercholesterolaemia (heterozygous variant) or combined (mixed) hyperlipidaemia

items.t: Adults with homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, as an adjunct to other lipid-lowering treatment (e.g. LDL apheresis) or if such treatment is unavailable.

src.q: Lipitor is also indicated to reduce total-C and LDL-C in adults with homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia

items.t: Prevention of cardiovascular events in adults estimated to be at high risk of a first cardiovascular event, alongside correction of other risk factors.

src.q: Prevention of cardiovascular events in adult patients estimated to have a high risk for a first cardiovascular event

items.t: Children: use only by physicians experienced in treating paediatric hyperlipidaemia, with regular re-evaluation.

src.q: Paediatric use should only be carried out by physicians experienced in the treatment of paediatric hyperlipidaemia

items.t: General: usual starting dose 10 mg once a day; adjust at intervals of 4 weeks or more; maximum 80 mg once a day. Patient should follow a cholesterol-lowering diet.

src.q: The usual starting dose is 10 mg once a day. Adjustment of dose should be made at intervals of 4 weeks or more. The maximum dose is 80 mg once a day.

items.t: Primary hypercholesterolaemia and mixed hyperlipidaemia: most patients are controlled on 10 mg once a day; maximum response usually within 4 weeks.

src.q: The majority of patients are controlled with Lipitor 10 mg once a day.

items.t: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (adults): start 10 mg daily, adjust every 4 weeks to 40 mg daily; then either increase to a maximum of 80 mg daily or combine 40 mg once daily with a bile acid sequestrant.

src.q: Patients should be started with Lipitor 10 mg daily. Doses should be individualised and adjusted every 4 weeks to 40 mg daily.
either the dose may be increased to a maximum of 80 mg daily or a bile acid sequestrant may be combined with 40 mg atorvastatin once daily

items.t: Homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia: 10 to 80 mg daily (limited data), as an adjunct to other lipid-lowering treatment.

src.q: The dose of atorvastatin in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia is 10 to 80 mg daily

items.t: Prevention of cardiovascular disease: 10 mg/day was used in primary prevention trials; higher doses may be needed to reach guideline cholesterol levels.

src.q: In the primary prevention trials the dose was 10 mg/day. Higher doses may be necessary in order to attain (LDL-) cholesterol levels according to current guidelines.

items.t: Maximum 20 mg/day with elbasvir/grazoprevir or letermovir; not recommended with letermovir plus ciclosporin.

src.q: the dose of atorvastatin should not exceed 20 mg/day
Use of atorvastatin is not recommended in patients taking letermovir co-administered with ciclosporin

items.t: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, 10 years and above: start 10 mg per day; may increase to 80 mg daily by response and tolerability, adjusting at intervals of 4 weeks or more.

src.q: For patients with Heterozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia aged 10 years and above, the recommended starting dose of atorvastatin is 10 mg per day
The dose may be increased to 80 mg daily, according to the response and tolerability.

items.t: Not indicated below 10 years of age; no dose recommendation can be made (only limited data in ages 6 to 10).

src.q: Atorvastatin is not indicated in the treatment of patients below the age of 10 years.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to atorvastatin or any excipient.

src.q: with hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1

items.t: Active liver disease or unexplained persistent serum transaminases above 3 times the upper limit of normal.

src.q: with active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases exceeding 3 times the upper limit of normal

items.t: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, and women of child-bearing potential not using appropriate contraception.

src.q: during pregnancy, while breast-feeding and in women of child-bearing potential not using appropriate contraceptive measures

items.t: With the hepatitis C antivirals glecaprevir/pibrentasvir.

src.q: treated with the hepatitis C antivirals glecaprevir/pibrentasvir

items.t: Muscle effects: can cause myalgia, myositis and myopathy that may progress to rhabdomyolysis. Prescribe with caution if there are pre-disposing factors for rhabdomyolysis.

src.q: may in rare occasions affect the skeletal muscle and cause myalgia, myositis, and myopathy that may progress to rhabdomyolysis
Atorvastatin should be prescribed with caution in patients with pre-disposing factors for rhabdomyolysis.

items.t: Measure CK before starting in: renal impairment, hypothyroidism, personal/family history of hereditary muscle disorders, previous muscle toxicity with a statin or fibrate, previous liver disease and/or substantial alcohol use; consider in people over 70. Do not start if baseline CK is above 5 times ULN.

src.q: A CK level should be measured before starting statin treatment in the following situations: - Renal impairment - Hypothyroidism
If CK levels are significantly elevated (> 5 times ULN) at baseline, treatment should not be started.

items.t: Use with caution in people who drink substantial quantities of alcohol and/or have a history of liver disease.

src.q: Lipitor should be used with caution in patients who consume substantial quantities of alcohol and/or have a history of liver disease.

items.t: After recent stroke or TIA, 80 mg was linked to more haemorrhagic stroke; in people with prior haemorrhagic stroke or lacunar infarct, the benefit-risk of 80 mg is uncertain and haemorrhagic stroke risk should be carefully considered.

src.q: For patients with prior haemorrhagic stroke or lacunar infarct, the balance of risks and benefits of atorvastatin 80 mg is uncertain

items.t: Systemic fusidic acid: atorvastatin must not be given with it or within 7 days of stopping it; stop the statin during fusidic acid treatment.

src.q: Atorvastatin must not be co-administered with systemic formulations of fusidic acid or within 7 days of stopping fusidic acid treatment.

items.t: Statins can raise blood glucose; people at risk of diabetes (fasting glucose 5.6 to 6.9 mmol/L, BMI>30kg/m2, raised triglycerides, hypertension) should be monitored. This is not a reason to stop the statin.

src.q: Patients at risk (fasting glucose 5.6 to 6.9 mmol/L, BMI>30kg/m2, raised triglycerides, hypertension) should be monitored both clinically and biochemically according to national guidelines.

items.t: Myasthenia gravis: statins may cause or worsen myasthenia gravis or ocular myasthenia; stop if symptoms get worse. MHRA: advise patients with myasthenia gravis to watch for worsening symptoms.

src.q: Lipitor should be discontinued in case of aggravation of symptoms.
advise patients with pre-existing myasthenia gravis to be alert to aggravation of symptoms while taking a statin

items.t: Interstitial lung disease has been reported; stop the statin if it is suspected.

src.q: If it is suspected a patient has developed interstitial lung disease, statin therapy should be discontinued.

items.t: Contains lactose: people with rare hereditary galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it.

src.q: Lipitor contains lactose.

items.t: Chewable tablets contain aspartame, a source of phenylalanine: may be harmful for people with phenylketonuria.

src.q: Lipitor chewable tablet contains aspartame which is a source of phenylalanine. May be harmful for people with phenylketonuria.

items.t: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. clarithromycin): avoid if possible. If unavoidable, consider lower starting and maximum atorvastatin doses with clinical monitoring.

src.q: should be avoided if possible. In cases where co-administration of these medicinal products with atorvastatin cannot be avoided lower starting and maximum doses of atorvastatin should be considered

items.t: Clarithromycin: SPS advises avoiding it with atorvastatin; consider pausing atorvastatin for the course; if both must be used, maximum atorvastatin 20 mg daily. MHRA (2008 article) also says do not exceed 20 mg atorvastatin daily with clarithromycin.

src.q: Avoid the use of clarithromycin with atorvastatin and use a non-interacting antibiotic if possible.
Use a lower dose of atorvastatin (maximum 20mg daily) if concurrent administration is unavoidable.
Clarithromycin: do not exceed 20 mg atorvastatin daily

items.t: Warfarin / coumarin anticoagulants: check prothrombin time before starting atorvastatin and often enough early on; repeat if the atorvastatin dose is changed or stopped. MHRA: monitor INR before starting and regularly, especially with dose changes.

src.q: prothrombin time should be determined before starting atorvastatin in patients taking coumarin anticoagulants
Monitor INR before starting treatment and regularly during treatment, especially with dose changes

items.t: CYP3A4 inducers such as St John's Wort can reduce atorvastatin levels.

src.q: inducers of cytochrome P450 3A (e.g. efavirenz, rifampin, St. John's Wort) can lead to variable reductions in plasma concentrations of atorvastatin

items.t: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. erythromycin, diltiazem, verapamil, fluconazole): consider a lower maximum dose and monitor.

src.q: a lower maximum dose of atorvastatin should be considered and appropriate clinical monitoring of the patient is recommended when concomitantly used with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors

items.t: Amlodipine and magnesium/aluminium hydroxide antacid: small changes in atorvastatin exposure; no specific recommendation in the SmPC.

src.q: Amlodipine 10 mg, single dose 80 mg, SD 1.18 No specific recommendation.

items.t: Avoid large quantities of grapefruit juice.

src.q: Concomitant intake of large quantities of grapefruit juice and atorvastatin is not recommended.

items.t: No dose adjustment needed in renal impairment. Renal impairment is a reason to measure CK before starting.

src.q: Renal impairment No adjustment of dose is required
A CK level should be measured before starting statin treatment in the following situations: - Renal impairment

items.t: SPS (all statins): if eGFR is less than 30 mL/min/1.73m2, check the dose with a renal specialist.

src.q: If eGFR less than 30mL/min/1.73m2 check dose with renal specialist.

items.t: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; contraindicated in active liver disease.

src.q: Lipitor should be used with caution in patients with hepatic impairment
Lipitor is contraindicated in patients with active liver disease

items.t: SPS: statins are not recommended in unexplained active liver disease or unexplained ALT/AST above 3 x ULN. In stable/chronic liver disease they can be used with caution; consider a lower starting dose such as atorvastatin 20 mg daily with gradual increase.

src.q: Statins are not recommended in patients with: unexplained active liver disease or, unexplained elevations of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) that are greater than 3 x the upper limit of normal (ULN).
consider a lower dose of a high-intensity statin, such as atorvastatin 20 mg daily or rosuvastatin 10 mg daily, with gradual dose escalation

items.t: Contraindicated in pregnancy; do not use in women who are pregnant, trying to become pregnant or who suspect pregnancy. Suspend for the duration of pregnancy.

src.q: Lipitor is contraindicated during pregnancy
Treatment with Lipitor should be suspended for the duration of pregnancy

items.t: BUMPS: statins are usually avoided in pregnancy; as a precaution most women are advised to stop statins three months before trying to conceive and during pregnancy.

src.q: Statins are usually avoided in pregnancy if possible as there is not enough information to say they are safe for the baby.
As a precaution, most women are advised to stop taking statins for three months before trying to conceive, and during pregnancy.

items.t: SmPC: contraindicated during breastfeeding; women taking atorvastatin should not breastfeed.

src.q: Atorvastatin is contraindicated during breast-feeding

items.t: SPS (differs from SmPC): atorvastatin is a preferred statin and can be used with caution while breastfeeding, with infant monitoring (feeding, growth, weight gain; diarrhoea, constipation, irritability). Postponing therapy until after exclusive breastfeeding is preferred if possible.

src.q: Atorvastatin can be used with caution while breastfeeding, but infant monitoring is still required.
if possible, the preferred option would be to postpone lipid-lowering therapy until after the exclusive breastfeeding period

items.t: Women of child-bearing potential should use appropriate contraception during treatment.

src.q: Women of child-bearing potential should use appropriate contraceptive measures during treatment

items.t: No effect on male or female fertility in animal studies.

src.q: In animal studies atorvastatin had no effect on male or female fertility

items.t: Common: nasopharyngitis, allergic reactions, hyperglycaemia, headache, pharyngolaryngeal pain, epistaxis, constipation, flatulence, dyspepsia, nausea, diarrhoea, myalgia, arthralgia, pain in extremity, muscle spasms, joint swelling, back pain, abnormal liver function tests, raised CK.

src.q: Common: nasopharyngitis.
Common: constipation, flatulence, dyspepsia, nausea, diarrhoea.
Common: myalgia, arthralgia, pain in extremity, muscle spasms, joint swelling, back pain.
Common: liver function test abnormal, blood creatine kinase increased.

items.t: Rhabdomyolysis / myopathy: stop if CK is above 10 x ULN or rhabdomyolysis is diagnosed or suspected; stop if CK above 5 x ULN with muscle symptoms.

src.q: Atorvastatin must be discontinued if clinically significant elevation of CK levels (> 10 x ULN) occur, or if rhabdomyolysis is diagnosed or suspected.
If these levels are found to be significantly elevated (> 5 times ULN), treatment should be stopped.

items.t: Immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (very rare): persistent proximal weakness and raised CK despite stopping the statin.

src.q: There have been very rare reports of an immune mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) during or after treatment with some statins.

items.t: Liver injury: hepatitis (uncommon), cholestasis (rare), hepatic failure (very rare). If transaminases above 3 x ULN persist, reduce dose or stop.

src.q: Uncommon: hepatitis. Rare: cholestasis. Very rare: hepatic failure.
Should an increase in transaminases of greater than 3 times the upper limit of normal (ULN) persist, reduction of dose or withdrawal of Lipitor is recommended

items.t: Rare severe skin reactions and angioedema (angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis including erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis); anaphylaxis very rare.

src.q: Rare: angioneurotic oedema, dermatitis bullous including erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis

items.t: Interstitial lung disease: stop the statin if suspected.

src.q: If it is suspected a patient has developed interstitial lung disease, statin therapy should be discontinued.

items.t: Liver function tests before starting and periodically thereafter.

src.q: Liver function tests should be performed before the initiation of treatment and periodically thereafter.

items.t: SPS before starting: ALT or AST, blood pressure, BMI, lipid profile (non-fasting), serum creatinine or eGFR, HbA1c. Consider CK if persistent muscle symptoms and TSH if thyroid symptoms.

src.q: Before starting Required Baseline ALT or AST Blood pressure Body mass index

items.t: SPS: ALT or AST and lipids between months 2 and 3; then consider annually (ALT/AST after the first year only if indicated).

src.q: Required Between months 2 and 3 ALT or AST
Annually ALT or AST · repeat after first year only if indicated

items.t: Measure CK if muscle pain, cramps or weakness occur; do not measure after strenuous exercise.

src.q: If such symptoms occur whilst a patient is receiving treatment with atorvastatin, their CK levels should be measured.

items.t: SPS: stop or do not start a statin if ALT or AST are greater than 3 times ULN, or if CK is greater than 5 times ULN.

src.q: Stop existing statin or do not initiate new statin if ALT or AST are greater than 3 times upper limit of normal (ULN).
Stop existing statin or do not initiate statin if creatine kinase (CK) greater than 5 times ULN.

items.t: Oral, once daily at any time of day, with or without food.

src.q: Each daily dose of atorvastatin is given all at once and may be given at any time of day with or without food.

items.t: Chewable tablets can be chewed or swallowed whole with water, at any time of day, with or without food.

src.q: Lipitor chewable tablets can be chewed or swallowed whole with a drink of water, and can be taken at any time of day, with or without food.

items.t: Report muscle pain, cramps or weakness promptly, especially with malaise or fever.

src.q: Patients must be asked to promptly report muscle pain, cramps, or weakness especially if accompanied by malaise or fever.
